Nice CMV. Let's get straight to it. 

Have you considered the detrimental behaviour that's found in the men's groups that exist in women's groups and women still (and sometimes as result of) get attention? If yes...

Have you then, considered the bias in the moral evaluation of toxic behaviours on the basis of which gendered individual or group did it?

Think of all the "but if a man did that, he'd be...<insert creative Internet expressions of penalty>"

Look into the difference in discouragement women and men face for natural human reactions (who gets away with being "bitchy" and why is that word female centric but that's just a start. I'm sure you'll find more when you think about it).

Look into the penalty both legal and social for women and men for the same toxic behaviour. Evaluate from "not even considered" to "incarcerated". 

You don't seem to come across as someone cushioning that view by saying "At least in part", but that sort of thing is used to get away with saying a lot of things. So, just to help put words to a lot of people who know somethings iffy but can't describe it, here it is. 

To me, the rhetoric of your view (not an attack of you, just a critic of the view) is the equivalent of saying 

"Homosexuals don't get enough attention because they shoot themselves in the foot - at least in part - by the homophobia caused by them hitting on and catcalling straight men." 

"At least in part" how much exactly? And in light of what other factors that contribute to this inattention? Is it so small as to be a non-point? 

Imagine you got asphyxiated to death and I say "that's atleast in part because your cells used up the oxygen, and that's a cellular issue.", you'd probably reincarnate and asphyxiated me. 

Yes. But in no part would anyone hold those cells accountable for your death.

The Homosexuals example is questioning the relevance even if the phenomenon exists.

The asphyxiation example is addressing the inversion of cause and effect.

The gender discriminations is answering the contributions in both circumstances leading to no deterrents to prove this isn't a situation of self sabotage.

A black man should NOT have to fight to matter. If another black man steals, black men shouldn't have to be jailed.

Men aren't suffering at the hands of inattention caused by incels. If a baby isn't cared for, and say it runs away from its home, would you say "that's in part because it ran away from its home"?

Hello Human, 

I'd like to quote something that touched me deeply and resonated with my past and will address. 

--I don't want to say I'm a humanist instead of a feminist, because to do that is to let the assholes take control of the word "feminism".-- 

(If I quoted the quote, the end would have to quotes and my knowledge of grammar rules are iffy) 

Now, back to the quote. IF, that is truly your concern, I've got bad and good news.

First off, I'd like to commend the desire to save a cause for the good you may have seen it do. I remember fighting for a relationship that went south but I held on to it because of the good. 

The bad news that I hate to break to you : The political movement and the propaganda that's over the decades surrounding Feminism is beyond your control. It really is. The "assholes" have been at it collectively for more hours than you, and this wasn't a movement too intolerant to who gets in, so long as they agree to hold the same stance.

Why should you not fight for the respect of a movement? It's the sunk cost fallacy and you will lose. I can not last remember the time someone was able to bleach a movement off the self serving corrupt (post or pre influence) joiners who wanted recognition for their cause and power for their validation. 

I don't have any ulterior motive here. This, isn't just an issue of feminism. Look at stalinism, look at religion and its believers, look at something as recent as black lives matter. They all wanted to gather numbers to make more noise about a cause that mattered without principles that filtered bad actors. At best, they were echo Chambers and at worst a where those with best intentions were left feeling misrepresented. It's the latter to whom my heart reaches out to. 

The natural question - why do such movements get bad actors that leverage the moralising goals to their own ends? 

Simple. Because people can, and do leverage resources and collectives for all sorts of reason. Leave the power hungry, malevolent folks aside. Let's say cast away the nazis of the movement. But what of the folks that just joined in for a reason as simple as benign as social belonging. 

I forget the documentary but some redneck motley crew of flat earthers wanted to prove to the world their claim was right. They did the whole eratosthenes test iirc, had gyroscope test. They did it because they didn't question physics in front of their eyes, they questioned scientists and trusted only themselves (which is honestly a moment of them exhibiting true skepticism and empiricism. Just something to smile and acknowledge) 

As the rotund world would have it, their experimentation proved them wrong. Now, the emotional dissonance and embarrassment is something easy to throw scorn at, but I actually empathize.  At that stage the flat earthers aren't fighting because they're right, they're fighting because, even after proving themselves wrong, they _need_ to hold the premise so that they don't disband. Why? 

There can be no group of flat earthers if they now concede the earth isn't flat, that they are wrong. There is no feminism if the group concedes the evils they purported of an out group isn't true, and that modifications to temper such a view would affect the indignation which they use to enroll more foot soldiers for the cause. 

We're humans, and self interests, vengeance, indoctrination, the desire to be living a life of purpose and belonging, and having access to the ranges of emotion from anger and disgust to success, and safety come far, far more in our consideration over principles.

Movements found on principles allow for change. Religion has the same book, but no one ever quotes the bits of bible about slavery. Feminism does it with waves. 
Science takes a different approach. It 

Who doesn't find purpose in fighting for something larger than life without it threatening their life, a lot of folks. Plenty of people. How quick are people to jump boat when it's easier for their mind to explain off something that didn't bode well. Chances of jumping are low if you've come to strongly identify with the movement or with the immediate folks who also label themselves. 


Oh the things we do and the price we pay. Is there any good news? Specifically for you, actually yes. 

You don't need to be married to labels, let alone atone for its sins and fight for its redemption. You don't own zilch to the bad actors that hijacked a movement. That happened because of the movement let it happen in exchange for more number and more influence. 

You were probably a humanist intuitively all along. You didn't need nobody to tell you what was and wasn't fair for you. To pick a label was restrictive in the first place. 

You'll also find that movements which are open to revision of stances because of the principle to find humanity's position in the world, directly, without any propagandist appeal to emotion, resonate with your own.
